Public comment period opens for feedback on LSOG Forest Conservation Strategies draft document
August 18, 2026
The Department of Agriculture, Conservation, and Forestry (DACF) has opened a public comment period on a draft document that identifies conservation strategies for late-successional and old-growth (LSOG) forests in Maine.  Maine's 132nd Legislature passed LD 1529, charging the DACF with developing a comprehensive report on statewide strategies to enhance the conservation of LSOG forests, including the management of transitioning late-successional forests. Through a work group, the DACF has engaged a broad range of perspectives to help develop the draft document.
Public feedback is an important step in preparing the LSOG Conservation Strategies document for the Maine legislature, as it will further broaden feedback.  DACF released a draft document for public comment on the
LSOG work group website
on August 17:
LSOG Conservation Strategies Draft document for public comment (PDF)
. An
online form for submitting comments
is also provided at the LSOG work group website. Comments will be due by August 28 at 5 PM.

Public comment period opens for feedback on LSOG Forest Conservation Strategies draft document

August 18, 2026

The Department of Agriculture, Conservation, and Forestry (DACF) has opened a public comment period on a draft document that identifies conservation strategies for late-successional and old-growth (LSOG) forests in Maine. Maine's 132nd Legislature passed LD 1529, charging the DACF with developing a comprehensive report on statewide strategies to enhance the conservation of LSOG forests, including the management of transitioning late-successional forests. Through a work group, the DACF has engaged a broad range of perspectives to help develop the draft document.

Public feedback is an important step in preparing the LSOG Conservation Strategies document for the Maine legislature, as it will further broaden feedback. DACF released a draft document for public comment on the LSOG work group website on August 17: LSOG Conservation Strategies Draft document for public comment (PDF). An online form for submitting comments is also provided at the LSOG work group website. Comments will be due by August 28 at 5 PM.

Natural Resources Disaster Relief Assistance Program (NRDRAP) applications Open today, Friday, August 14
August 14, 2026
The Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry (DACF) is opening applications for the Natural Resources Disaster Relief Assistance Program (NRDRAP) today, Friday, August 14, 2026.
Maine farmers, forestry businesses, aquaculture producers, and other eligible producers who experienced weather-related losses in 2023 or 2024 may qualify for financial assistance.
Eligible losses may include crop loss, aquaculture loss, standing timber loss, harvested timber loss, on-farm and forestry infrastructure loss, and bare-ground practices necessary to mitigate land loss.
Application period
: August 14, 2026, through November 6, 2026.
Applications will be accepted through the online portal
. Paper applications are available upon request.
Producers can prepare now
. Applicants are encouraged to begin gathering documentation, including:
Ownership or lease documentation
Parcel ID information
FSA Farm Number, if applicable
Tax or business identification information
Photos or records documenting damage
Other records related to weather-related losses in 2023 and/or 2024 
DACF will provide technical assistance throughout the application period. Virtual office hours will be held every Friday from 11:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. beginning August 14.
For updates, eligibility information, and application details, visit
maine.gov/dacf/nrdrap
, email
NRDRA.DACF@maine.gov
, or call (207) 530-3144.
Back to Top

Do you work in Maine's agriculture, fishing, or forestry industries? Your Experience Matters.
August 3, 2026
Survey to Help Shape Mental Health & Wellness Resources for Maine's Heritage Industries
If you work in Maine's agriculture, fishing, or forestry industries, your experience matters. Take this anonymous 10-minute survey by August 31, 2026, to help shape recommendations that will strengthen mental health and wellness resources for Maine's heritage industries. Every response helps ensure the recommendations reflect the real experiences and needs of those who do this work every day.
